record.paper_title: Confinement of color: open problems and perspectives.
record.original_question: What is the correct dual description of QCD confinement: which dual symmetry is broken or realized in the confining vacuum, and which topological excitations are the relevant carriers of that dual order? More concretely, among candidates such as monopoles obtained through abelian projection and vortices associated with nontrivial topology, which excitations actually provide the mechanism of color confinement in 3+1 dimensions, and how should their symmetry properties be identified?

evidence.quote: The problem is then to identify the dual symmetry and the corresponding topological excitations.
Vortices could be relevant to confinement also in (3+1)d[11].
Understanding the relevant dual excitations and their symmetries amounts to under￾stand the mechanism of color confinement.

I think that a fair conclusion is that we do not know yet the dual excitations : we only know that they carry magnetic charge in all abelian projections, and that the confining vacuum is a dual superconductor in the confined phase , a property which disappears above the deconfining transition.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider SU(3) Yang–Mills theory (and, more generally, QCD with quarks) in 3+1 spacetime dimensions, regularized on a Euclidean lattice. It is widely conjectured that the confining vacuum admits a dual description, in which a global "dual" symmetry is realized differently in the confined and deconfined phases, with the confined phase characterized by condensation of topologically nontrivial excitations (a dual-superconductor-like picture). Two principal candidate classes of dual excitations have been proposed:

(a) Magnetic monopoles defined via abelian projection — i.e. the defects obtained after partially fixing the gauge so that an abelian subgroup U(1)^{N-1} ⊂ SU(N) remains, with monopole world-lines arising from the Dirac quantization condition on the residual abelian fluxes;

(b) Center vortices — closed two-dimensional world-sheets carrying flux in the center Z_N of the gauge group, associated with nontrivial π_1(SU(N)/Z_N) = Z_N topology, detected for instance via maximal center gauge and center projection.

The problem is to determine:

1. The correct dual global symmetry whose spontaneous breaking (or unbroken realization) characterizes the confining vacuum of 3+1 dimensional Yang–Mills theory, together with a gauge-invariant order parameter distinguishing the confined and deconfined phases.

2. Which class of topological excitations — abelian-projection monopoles, center vortices, some combination, or a different set of objects — provides the genuine carriers of this dual order, in the sense that their condensation (in the confined phase) and de-condensation (above the deconfining temperature) account for the area law of the fundamental Wilson loop and the linear quark–antiquark potential.

3. The precise symmetry properties (magnetic charge group, transformation laws under the proposed dual symmetry) of these excitations, and a demonstration — analytic or via lattice constructions — that they reproduce the observed confining and deconfining phases of pure SU(3) gauge theory.

Provide either a proof identifying the correct dual symmetry and dual excitations, or a rigorous argument ruling out one or both of the candidate mechanisms above.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and lattice studies (e.g. 2024 reviews on the confinement mechanism) continue to discuss both abelian-projection monopoles and center vortices as candidate dual excitations without a definitive identification. The dual-superconductor picture has substantial lattice support (monopole condensation correlates with confinement, and removing monopoles or vortices destroys the area law), but the precise dual symmetry and the identification of the true dual excitations in 3+1 dimensional QCD remain unsettled.

status_evidence.title: What do we know about the confinement mechanism?
status_evidence.snippet: Despite notable progress... confinement is still an active field of research and debate.
status_evidence.claim: As of late 2024, the confinement mechanism—including the choice between monopole- and vortex-based dual descriptions—remains an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic monopoles and magnetic vortices
status_evidence.snippet: The world lines of the magnetic monopoles lie on the world surfaces of the vortices and reflect their color structure.
status_evidence.claim: Monopole and vortex pictures are studied as complementary but not yet unified into a single accepted dual description.

status_evidence.title: QCD Vacuum as Dual Superconductor: Quark Confinement and Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Dual superconductor picture of QCD vacuum and its topological foundations.
status_evidence.claim: Dual-superconductor picture is supported but the precise dual excitations are still under investigation.
